gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the REDTIGER F77's SD slot cannot record. Redtiger's statement, relayed by DashCamTalk tester rcg530, is that it 'can only be used for downloading videos, not for recording'. So the 128 GB eMMC holds the entire loop, and the tester measured eMMC copies over USB-C at only about 18.41 MB/s.
standout_why: I tried to open every cited rival page, but none loaded: 70mai.store M500 and ddpai.com/en-us Z90 Master returned HTTP 429, incartec.com had a TLS certificate error, shopredtiger.shop did not resolve, and the manuals.plus M800 PDF was compressed binary I could not read. The comparison is therefore against the result titles and ChatGPT's answer. ChatGPT told the shopper the F77 has 'no SD card slot', which is wrong. No result title says the slot exists but only backs up eMMC files and cannot extend recording, or how slowly footage comes off the built-in memory. The rival DDPAI and 70mai titles only advertise 'built-in eMMC' and say nothing about how footage gets off the device.
decides: This confirms that 'built-in memory' means recording capacity is fixed when you buy the camera. On the F77 an SD card cannot add recording time, so buy the larger eMMC variant if you want a longer loop. Getting footage out is slow: by my arithmetic, copying the full 128 GB at the measured 18.41 MB/s takes about 1.9 h. On the 70mai M500, the manual describes the eMMC as built in, and the footage path it describes is the 70mai app over the camera's Wi-Fi hotspot. Shoppers who want both built-in memory and an expandable or swappable fallback should look at the DDPAI eMMC + microSD models (Z90 Pro and N5 Pro, both already listed on Dealectric). I could not open DDPAI's own wording on how its D²save fallback works.

findings.label: Where video is recorded
findings.value: 128 GB eMMC; 'Videos are written to this storage'
findings.source_title: Redtiger F77 - 2-Channel - 4K Front + 4K Rear - Testing / Review - RCG (DashCamTalk)
findings.note: Posted by tester rcg530 on 2024-12-03 in their hands-on review thread.

findings.label: SD card slot function
findings.value: Backup/download only, not recording. Redtiger: 'The SD card slot on the device can only be used for downloading videos, not for recording.'
findings.source_title: Redtiger F77 - 2-Channel - 4K Front + 4K Rear - Testing / Review - RCG (DashCamTalk)
findings.note: Redtiger's reply as relayed by rcg530 on 2024-12-06. rcg530 adds: 'The SD card memory slot can be used to backup video files from the eMMC storage.' This contradicts ChatGPT's 'no SD card slot'.

findings.label: USB-C transfer from eMMC
findings.value: 18.41 MB/s copy speed; over USB-C the camera asks whether to mount the eMMC or the SD card as a drive
findings.source_title: Redtiger F77 - 2-Channel - 4K Front + 4K Rear - Testing / Review - RCG (DashCamTalk)
findings.note: Measured by rcg530 (posted 2024-12-16), who called it much slower than the other devices tested. My arithmetic: 128 GB ÷ 18.41 MB/s ≈ 6,950 s ≈ 1.9 h to copy a full eMMC.

findings.label: Storage type
findings.value: Built-in eMMC; 'The eMMC (Embedded Multi Media Card) is built in the dash cam for storage.' Capacity is printed on the camera label and the box
findings.note: Text of 70mai's own M500 manual (79 pages), English section.

findings.label: Operating temperature
findings.value: -10 °C to 60 °C ('Do not use the dash cam in environments with temperatures over 60°C or below -10°C.')
findings.note: From the manual's safety section. This is the limit for the whole camera, eMMC included.

findings.label: Footage access and storage reset
findings.value: 'This product needs to be used in conjunction with the 70mai app.' The phone joins the camera's own Wi-Fi hotspot (default password 12345678; Android 4.4 / iOS 9.0 or later). Pressing the button 4 times = 'Format the built-in memory card'
findings.source_title: 70mai M500 Manual de Instrucciones, page 5 Button Functions (ManualsLib)
findings.note: This manual page does not describe a USB or card path for getting footage off the camera; the app over Wi-Fi is the path it describes.
